messages.subject: Re: modular GPA?
parts:
On Wed, Apr 5, 2023, 10:54 AM Jayme Massim <massim...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello all, I would like some help with the best way to analyze my data set:I have a set of 3D TPS  files (116 points) generated with Morphodig software for 3D surfaces of 26 species of pitvipers skulls. The idea of my PHD is to test if the skull shape is driven by diet and living habits (using just adult specimens).
lso test if allometric patterns are driven by diet and living habits  (using my whole sample).
My question is specifically about GPA, because gnathic bones in snakes aren't static and can be in different positions on each 3D surface, different from the brain case.

Is there some way to analyze all 116 points together, that is, a GPA that gives the same configuration for each module, or is it better to separate and analyze each bone separated?

Thanks for your attention.

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Re: modular GPA?
parts:
The R-package ‘ShapeRotator’ provides a 3D version of my fixed.angle approach (Adams 1999), which was originally proposed for 2D data.

 

Dean
